```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# Bash chunks are a record of commands you ran in the Terminal. Knitting shows
# them but doesn't run them again.
knitr::opts_hooks$set(engine = function(options) {
  if (options$engine == "bash") options$eval <- FALSE
  options
})
```

```{r read-length-histogram}
library(tidyverse)

rl_data <- read_tsv(
  "read_lengths.txt",
  col_names = c("id", "length"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

ggplot(rl_data, aes(x = length / 1000)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2) +
  xlab("Read Length (kb)") +
  ylab("Number of Reads") +
  ggtitle("Read Length Distribution of Mock Metagenome")
```

```{r read-n50}
total_len <- sum(rl_data$length)

rl_data |>
  arrange(desc(length)) |>
  mutate(cumsum = cumsum(length)) |>
  filter(cumsum > total_len / 2) |>
  head(n = 1)
```

```{r gc-histogram}
library(tidyverse)

gc <- read_tsv(
  "assembly_check/assembly.gc.tsv",
  col_names = c("#seq_name", "length", "GC"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

info <- read_tsv(
  "flye_metagenome/mock/assembly_info.txt",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

gc_info <- left_join(info, gc, by = "#seq_name")

ggplot(gc_info, aes(x = GC)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, colour = "black") +
  xlab("GC Content") +
  ylab("Number of Contigs") +
  ggtitle("GC Content of Metagenome Contigs")
```
```{r gc-vs-coverage}
gc_info |>
  filter(GC < 0.8, cov. < 25) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = GC, y = cov.)) +
 geom_point(aes(size = length.x), alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title = "GC Content vs Coverage of Metagenome Contigs",
    x = "GC Content",
    y = "Coverage Depth (×)",
    size = "Contig Length (bp)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r assembly-completeness}
assembly_length <- sum(gc_info$length.x)
reference_length <- 24095709

completeness <- (assembly_length / reference_length) * 100

cat("Assembly length:", assembly_length, "bp\n")
cat("Reference length:", reference_length, "bp\n")
cat("Proportion of reference:", round(completeness, 2), "%\n")
```
```
### CheckM results and interpretation

CheckM v1.2.2 was used to estimate genome-bin completeness
and contamination using lineage-specific marker genes.

The analysis evaluated seven genome files, including six
MetaBAT2 bins and the separately extracted contig_43.

The highest-quality genome had an estimated completeness
of 99.87% and contamination of 0.71%.

Another bin, metabat.5, had 67.68% completeness and
0.00% detected contamination.

Several other bins had low completeness (7.48–18.26%),
indicating that substantial portions of their estimated
genomes were missing.

Overall, the metagenomic assembly and binning recovered
genomes of varying quality. Low detected contamination
does not necessarily indicate a complete genome.
